evidence.note: Maintained an explicit running 'still need' inventory of subsystems (CopyObject, multipart, bucket configs, admin API, lifecycle worker, catch-all route) as it built, marking each area off — a usable, continuously-updated checklist.

Prolonged loop on the SigV4 query-string SignatureDoesNotMatch bug; repeatedly re-attempted the same failing sed/replace edits and re-diagnosed before recognizing (step 74) the piecemeal approach wasn't landing and switching to a full function rewrite. Recognition of the stuck state came eventually, not early.

Granular contract-level tracking: diffed the required data-testid list against app.js and caught loading-indicator existing only as CSS, not as a testid element — fine-grained coverage reconciliation.

Flagged lifecycle-worker and notification-worker runtime verification as 'still need to verify' at step 110, but the final self-assessment claims both complete with checkmarks without an observed runtime test — a mild silent gap dropped at the horizon.
Final assessment is a detailed, itemized done-list across all subsystems with per-behavior checkmarks (error codes, ETag, ranges), demonstrating sustained situational awareness of the whole surface.

reasoning: The agent kept an accurate, granular done-vs-remaining picture across all ~dozen subsystems and down to specific contract items (error codes, testids, ETag/range rules), which exceeds the level-5 anchor. It fell short of 8-10 because it burned roughly 25 steps circling the same SigV4/parse_qs mismatch with repeated identical edits before naming the impasse and changing approach, and because a flagged lifecycle/notification verification was left unconfirmed yet marked complete at the horizon. That combination — strong granular coverage tracking plus somewhat delayed thrashing recognition and one mild silent gap — places it at 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
